findings.observed: Quiet ivory paving has a narrow straight change in brush-field brightness at the true column join, clearest just below row 1. This is not a paving groove. No missing geometry observed.
findings.recommendation: Constrain a local low-frequency color/texture transition to the stone plane; preserve the existing grooves and tree-shadow boundaries.

findings.observed: A straight vertical light/dark slice passes through several otherwise continuous green leaf lobes and the crown undergrowth. The line is grid-aligned and not the contour of one leaf; no large missing lobe is observed.
findings.recommendation: Match lighting and color across this narrow seam while following existing leaf shapes; do not replace the seam with new leaf masses or blur leaf outlines.

findings.observed: Orange planter top and front face change luminance along a straight vertical cut; the top white bevel is substantially aligned. The horizontal row join also crosses the same curved block. This rectangular lighting split is unrelated to its rounded corner geometry.
findings.recommendation: Use the same underlying orange plane and continuous white bevel; correct the local color field around the cross seam, then inspect the bevel at 1:1.

findings.observed: A faint straight tonal/material boundary is visible on otherwise continuous ivory stone around the row-3/row-4 intersection. Crossing grooves are largely continuous; no large gap observed.
findings.recommendation: Match restrained stone brush scale and mean color locally without broad blurring or shifting the diagonal grooves.

findings.observed: At the guide-band end, the diagonal white paving bevel and dark groove make an abrupt approximately 2–3 px backward step. Both contour and dark channel change at the same vertical boundary; this is not normal material variation.
findings.recommendation: Repair the short bevel and groove within this small ROI, continuing the established slope through x3187; preserve the broad stone texture and do not adjust the whole cell.

diagnosticOnly.note: Minimum-row samples support the viewed step; they are not a full subpixel geometry fit.

findings.observed: The three row-1 intersections show a horizontal tonal/brush-field join. It is strongest through the crown in c2, where the grid-aligned step cuts across independent leaves; the stone intersections are less pronounced.
findings.recommendation: Coordinate with the standard-horizontal reviewer. Correct color on each underlying surface and preserve leaf silhouettes and paving lines; these observations cover the three intersection crops only.

findings.observed: A straight row boundary crosses the tree shadow/stone in c1, the orange planter in c2, and the white wall/pillar base in c3. This crosses existing object shading rather than following physical contours.
findings.recommendation: Coordinate with the standard-horizontal reviewer and correct each surface independently; retain shadow shape and the stone/planter edges.

findings.observed: At c1 and c2, the stone above the row boundary has broader painterly patches while the lower field is smoother. c2 also has the V4 column transition. No missing diagonal groove is observed in these two intersection crops.
findings.recommendation: Coordinate with the standard-horizontal reviewer; reconcile brush scale and low-frequency color without repainting mapped line geometry.
